name: Vyrel Mate-Mint Surge
manufacturer: Vyrel Energy Systems (energy drink brand, Corponation subsidiary)
description: A carbonated mate-based soda with real yerba mate extract and cooling peppermint, positioned as a 'clean energy' alternative to synthetic stimulant drinks. Less aggressive than Vyrel's main energy line but with a devoted following among Tier 2-3 office workers.
flavor_profile: Earthy, grassy mate bitterness balanced with cool, clean mint, moderate carbonation, slightly astringent finish that wakes the palate — caffeinated without tasting medicinal
slogan: Real energy. Real ingredients. Real day.
cultural_context: Vyrel Mate-Mint sits in an interesting cultural position: too herbal and 'crunchy' for the hardcore energy drink crowd, but more affordable and edgy than the wellness sodas. It's the drink of Tier 2 data workers and low-level BCI technicians — people who need to stay sharp but can't afford Dravani's price point. Vyrel markets it with sponsored BCI-focus streamers.
story_hooks: Vyrel's yerba mate supply chain runs through a region of the former South American agricultural zones that is now a contested corponation territory — a supply chain disruption is coming, and Vyrel's logistics team is scrambling to find an alternative before the next quarter.

A Tier 2 BCI technician has been using Vyrel Mate-Mint cans to smuggle modified neural chips out of a corponation facility — the cans are a perfect size for the components, and the technician has been doing it for eight months without detection.

An independent study shows Vyrel Mate-Mint has measurably better cognitive effects than Vyrel's premium synthetic energy line — Vyrel's parent company is suppressing the study because it would cannibalize their higher-margin products.
